title: MSDE convenes ‘Kaushal Manthan’ Regional Conference of Skill Ministers in Kolkata
subtitle:
Shri Jayant Chaudhary calls for transforming ITIs into industry-responsive institutions linked with sustainable careers
States deliberate on PM-SETU, decentralised planning, industry partnerships and workforce mobility
body_text:
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) convened ‘Kaushal Manthan’, the Regional Conference of Skill Ministers in Kolkata today. The Conference brought together Ministers and senior officers from participating States and Union Territory to strengthen Centre–State coordination and advance an industry-connected, outcome-oriented skilling ecosystem.
The Conference was chaired by Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India.
It was attended by Shri Jagannath Chattopadhyay, Minister-in-charge- Higher Education Department and Technical Education, Training and Skill Development Department, Government of West Bengal; Shri Kunvarjibhai Mohanbhai Bavaliya, Minister of Labour, Skill Development and Employment Department, Government of Gujarat; Guru Khushwant Saheb, Minister for Skill Development, Technical Education & Employment and Scheduled Caste Development, Government of Chhattisgarh; Dr. Gotam Tetwal, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Skill Development and Employment, Government of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Sampad Chandra Swain, Minister of State (Independent Charge) Industries, Skill Development and Technical Education Government of Odisha and Dr HareKrishna Bera, MoS- Technical Education, Training and Skill Development department. Senior representatives from Goa, Jharkhand and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu also participated.
Addressing the Conference, Shri Jayant Chaudhary said, “India’s young people bring extraordinary ambition, adaptability and potential. Our responsibility is to connect that potential with future-ready, industry-valued skills and real opportunities. PM-SETU gives us a historic opportunity to reimagine ITIs as vibrant centres of excellence, innovation and aspiration. Achieving this will require strong convergence between the Centre, States, industry and training institutions, aligning policy, infrastructure and investment around the learner. Its success will ultimately be reflected in the careers, enterprises and upward mobility we enable”.
The Minister emphasised that the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) Scheme should be implemented as a comprehensive institutional reform. He encouraged States to align PM-SETU clusters with priority economic value chains, industrial corridors, MSME concentrations, emerging technologies and upcoming investments, with Spoke ITIs receiving dependable access to Hub laboratories, master trainers, career services and employer networks.
Referring to future-ready capabilities, Shri Chaudhary noted that over 2.10 lakh learners had enrolled under SOAR (Skilling for AI Readiness) by 16 July 2026. He stressed that AI learning must reach schools, ITIs and skill centres across districts, enabling young people not merely to use AI, but to apply, adapt and create with it.
The participating Ministers shared their States’ experiences and deliberated on ITI transformation, district-level planning, industry participation, integration of vocational and mainstream education, employability, entrepreneurship, inclusion and workforce mobility. They underlined the need to align skilling interventions with State economic priorities while maintaining common national standards for curriculum, assessment, certification and outcomes. Apprenticeship was also recognised as an important bridge between institutional training and the workplace.
Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, in her opening address, called for a unified Centre–State implementation architecture. She said that State Skill Policies, District Skill Development Plans and State Skill Development Plans should guide scheme targets, infrastructure investments, trainer deployment and employer partnerships.
During 2024–25, States and Union Territories submitted District Skill Development Plans and State Skill Development Plans. The Conference discussed strengthening these plans with district- and job role-wise demand, institutional capacity, trainer availability and local economic drivers, supported by functional District Skill Committees and annual action frameworks with clear ownership and measurable outcomes.
Shri Dilip Kumar, Director General, DGT reiterated that The transformation of ITIs under PM-SETU is not merely an infrastructure upgrade; it is a commitment to creating industry-responsive institutions that equip youth with future-ready skills, enhance employability, and support India's journey towards becoming a global talent hub.
Ms. Manasi Sahay Thakur, Joint Secretary, MSDE , made a presentation on PM-SETU, outlining the role of States in identifying clusters, onboarding Anchor Industry Partners, preparing State Implementation Plans and establishing effective governance and monitoring mechanisms.
The Conference also witnessed the launch of a pioneering international skilling programme for 600 OBC youth from Madhya Pradesh, approved by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and implemented by NSDC under the aegis of MSDE. The programme will provide foreign-language and destination-readiness training for opportunities in Japan and Germany across high-demand sectors including caregiving, hospitality, construction and manufacturing. Training will be delivered by NSDC International Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of NSDC.
The first-of-its-kind initiative will operate through a three-part blended-finance model comprising beneficiary participation, grant funding mobilised through the Social Stock Exchange, and outcome-based financing by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. The model connects specialised training with measurable outcomes and international employment pathways, offering a replicable approach for financing skilling and global mobility at scale.
An MoU for implementing the programme was exchanged between Shri Arun Kumar Pillai, CEO, NSDC, and Shri Sapan Jain, Additional Director, Dept of Backward Class and Minority Welfare, Govt. of Madhya Pradesh, in the presence of Shri Jayant Chaudhary and the participating dignitaries.
The Conference also discussed a unified framework for international mobility covering workforce identification, training, language proficiency, assessment, ethical recruitment and post-placement support. Caregiver mobility was identified as an immediate opportunity requiring destination-linked training, common standards, cultural readiness and worker safeguards.
Earlier in the day, Ms. Archana Mayaram, Economic Adviser, MSDE, presented an overview of MSDE’s key initiatives and the wider skilling and entrepreneurship ecosystem, including Skill India, entrepreneurship development and NCVET’s regulatory and quality-assurance framework. Principal Secretaries and Secretaries from the participating States and Union Territory subsequently presented their achievements, priorities and implementation experiences, followed by a roundtable discussion on Centre–State convergence.
Kaushal Manthan concluded with a shared commitment to strengthen Centre–State coordination, promote cross-State learning and review a focused set of implementation milestones and learner outcomes. MSDE reaffirmed its support to States through technical assistance and coordination with DGT, NSDC, NCVET and other concerned Ministries.
The Conference was also attended by Ms. Hena Usman and Ms. Manisha Sensarma, Senior Economic Adviser, MSDE along with senior officials from the Central and State Governments and partner institutions.

ministry.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

enrichment.summary: MSDE held the 'Kaushal Manthan' Regional Conference of Skill Ministers in Kolkata, chaired by Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary, to discuss Centre-State coordination on skilling under the PM-SETU scheme for ITI upgradation. The conference also saw the launch of an international skilling programme for 600 OBC youth from Madhya Pradesh for jobs in Japan and Germany, financed through a blended model, and updates showed over 2.10 lakh learners enrolled under the SOAR (Skilling for AI Readiness) initiative by mid-July 2026.
enrichment.context:
PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs) is a Centrally sponsored scheme aimed at modernising India's network of over 14,000 Industrial Training Institutes into hub-and-spoke clusters linked with industry, addressing long-standing criticism that ITI curricula are outdated and disconnected from employer needs. The scheme builds on earlier skilling missions like Skill India and works alongside institutions such as DGT (Directorate General of Training), NSDC (National Skill Development Corporation) and NCVET (National Council for Vocational Education and Training), which regulates certification standards. Decentralised planning through District and State Skill Development Plans reflects a broader governance shift toward aligning skilling with local economic drivers and job-role demand rather than uniform national targets.

The international mobility component, involving NSDC International Limited and a 'blended finance' model combining beneficiary contribution, Social Stock Exchange grants, and outcome-based state funding, signals growing government interest in structured labour migration pathways (especially caregiving) to aging-population countries like Japan and Germany, an area of increasing policy focus given India's demographic dividend and remittance potential. SOAR reflects the government's push to embed AI literacy into vocational training amid global concerns about automation's impact on employment.

options: Urban housing for economically weaker sections
prelims_questions.explanation: PM-SETU stands for Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs, a scheme to transform ITIs into industry-responsive institutions via a hub-and-spoke cluster model.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following bodies is responsible for regulatory and quality-assurance framework in India's vocational education and skilling ecosystem?
prelims_questions.explanation: The National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) is the regulator ensuring quality assurance in skill development and vocational education certification in India.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the PM-SETU scheme in transforming Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in India. What challenges must be addressed for successful Centre-State implementation of such skilling reforms?
Examine the potential and challenges of structured international labour mobility programmes for skilled and semi-skilled Indian youth, with reference to sectors like caregiving and hospitality.

study_notes.reason: The release carries testable factual details (PM-SETU scheme, NSDC International, SOAR enrolment figures, blended-finance model) alongside a genuine analytical theme of Centre-State convergence in skilling governance and structured international labour mobility, making it dual-use rather than tilted to one side.

prelims.point: PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme to upgrade India's 14,000+ ITIs into hub-and-spoke clusters linked with industry.
prelims.why_important: A newly prominent scheme name, objective and mechanism (hub-and-spoke ITI clusters) is classic prelims material for scheme-matching questions.

prelims.point: SOAR (Skilling for AI Readiness) initiative had enrolled over 2.10 lakh learners by 16 July 2026.
prelims.why_important: Scheme name and a specific data point could be used in a statement-based question on skilling initiatives.

prelims.point: NSDC International Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of NSDC, is implementing the international skilling programme for Madhya Pradesh youth.
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of institutional architecture under MSDE, including subsidiary bodies distinct from the parent NSDC.

prelims.point: NCVET (National Council for Vocational Education and Training) is the regulatory and quality-assurance body for skilling certification.
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing NCVET's regulatory role from NSDC's implementation role and DGT's training oversight is a common prelims trap on skilling institutions.

mains.point: PM-SETU signals a shift from uniform national ITI standards to demand-linked, industry-clustered vocational training aligned with local economic drivers.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers on reforming vocational education or improving industry-academia linkage in skill development.

mains.point: The blended-finance model (beneficiary contribution + Social Stock Exchange grants + outcome-based state funding) for international mobility is a replicable innovation in financing skilling and migration.
mains.theme: Innovative financing for skilling and migration
mains.analytical_use: Can be deployed in questions on innovative financing mechanisms for social sector programmes or on structured labour migration policy.

mains.point: Structured international mobility for caregiving and other sectors to ageing-population countries (Japan, Germany) reflects India's attempt to leverage demographic dividend via managed labour migration.
mains.theme: International labour mobility and demographic dividend
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for essay/GS2 questions on India's demographic dividend, remittances, and ethical recruitment frameworks for migrant workers.

mains.point: Embedding AI literacy into ITIs and skill centres through SOAR responds to concerns about automation's impact on employment and future job readiness.
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on AI's impact on employment and the need for reskilling to mitigate technological displacement.

mains.point: Centre-State coordination challenges in skilling — balancing common national standards for certification with State-specific economic priorities — remain a governance gap needing institutional architecture like District Skill Committees.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on cooperative federalism in social sector scheme implementation.
